title: Uniform mixing and $ε$-uniform mixing on cycles
abstract: We study continuous-time quantum walks on cycles. We prove two complementary results. Firstly, the cycle $C_9$ does not admit uniform mixing at any time. Using the similar idea and Dickson polynomials, we prove that $C_{15}$ does not admit uniform mixing at any time neither. Secondly, for every prime $p$, we show that the cycle $C_{p^2}$ admits $ε$-uniform mixing.
summary: This paper analyzes when continuous-time quantum walks on cycle graphs achieve perfect or near-perfect mixing. It proves that specific cycles, like $C_9$ and $C_{15}$, fail to mix uniformly at any time. Conversely, it establishes a positive result by showing that cycles of the form $C_{p^2}$ do admit $\epsilon$-uniform mixing for all primes $p$, using advanced spectral and algebraic methods.
main_problem: The study investigates the mixing properties (uniform and $\epsilon$-uniform) of continuous-time quantum walks evolving on cycle graphs ($C_n$).
main_result: The paper proves that $C_9$ and $C_{15}$ do not admit uniform mixing, while demonstrating that $C_{p^2}$ admits $\epsilon$-uniform mixing for any prime $p$.
method: The analysis combines spectral theory (using eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix) with advanced algebraic techniques like Gröbner basis calculations to establish necessary and sufficient conditions for perfect mixing.
model_or_system: The model is a continuous-time quantum walk on a cycle graph $C_n$, whose evolution is governed by the unitary operator $U(t) = \exp(itA)$, where $A$ is the adjacency matrix.
important_parameters: The cycle length $n$, specifically focusing on $C_9$, $C_{15}$, and $C_{p^2}$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies heavily on the spectral decomposition of the evolution operator and algebraic results concerning roots of unity.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes general conditions for uniform mixing using polynomial ideals (demonstrated via Gröbner bases for $C_9$ and $C_{15}$), followed by a separate analysis proving $\epsilon$-uniform mixing on $C_{p^2}$ using spectral approximation techniques.
why_interesting: The study of quantum walks' mixing properties is central to understanding quantum transport, decoherence, and the efficiency of quantum computation protocols in graph structures. The distinction between exact (uniform) and approximate ($\epsilon$-uniform) mixing provides deep insights into the underlying symmetries and algebraic structure of the graph.
